title: 枫桥夜泊
englishTitle: Mooring by Maple Bridge at Night
author: Zhang Ji

translation: The moon sets, crows caw, frost fills the sky
River maples and fishing lights face my sleepless sorrow
Outside the walls of Gusu stands Hanshan Temple
At midnight, the sound of its bell reaches my traveler's boat

annotations.乌啼: crows cawing — a sound associated with desolation
annotations.渔火: lights from fishing boats on the river
annotations.姑苏: Gusu — the ancient name of Suzhou
annotations.寒山寺: Hanshan Temple — a real temple you can still visit today
annotations.客船: traveler's boat — the poet is far from home

appreciation: A lone traveler moors his boat on a cold autumn night. Moon, crows, frost, river maples, fishing lights — every image deepens his insomnia. Then the midnight bell of Hanshan Temple drifts across the water, one of the most famous sounds in Chinese poetry. The temple in Suzhou still rings its bell for visitors today.
